title: WizardLM: Empowering Large Pre-Trained Language Models to Follow Complex Instructions
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to create large-scale, high-quality instruction-following datasets for large language models without relying heavily on expensive human annotation. The authors argue that human-written open-domain instruction datasets are costly to produce and tend to underrepresent highly complex instructions. Their central question is whether large language models themselves can be used to automatically generate more diverse and more difficult instructions, and whether training on those instructions improves downstream instruction-following performance.

To address this, the paper proposes Evol-Instruct, an automated data-generation framework that iteratively rewrites existing instructions to increase their complexity or breadth. The method includes in-depth evolution operations such as adding constraints, deepening questions, concretizing concepts, increasing reasoning steps, and complicating inputs, as well as in-breadth evolution to create new but related prompts. The authors use this process to evolve Alpaca instructions into a much larger dataset, then fine-tune LLaMA 13B to produce WizardLM. They also include filtering mechanisms to remove failed evolutions and evaluate the resulting model against baselines such as Alpaca and Vicuna using benchmark tests, GPT-4-based evaluation, and human judgments.

The paper is not an education study and does not examine students, teachers, or schools as participants. Instead, the empirical context is machine learning model development and evaluation using benchmark datasets, human annotators for evaluation, and LLM-generated instruction data. Human involvement appears only in model evaluation, where 10 annotators compare outputs, rather than in an educational intervention setting.

The main conclusion is that Evol-Instruct produces instruction data that substantially improves instruction-following model performance. WizardLM outperforms several open-source baselines on code, math, benchmark, GPT-4, and human evaluation measures, suggesting that automatically generated, complexity-controlled instruction datasets can be more effective than existing machine-generated or human-collected alternatives for supervised fine-tuning. The authors also conclude that instruction complexity is an important factor in improving model performance, while noting limitations in evaluation scalability and coverage.

identified_tools.name: WizardLM
identified_tools.description: A named instruction-following large language model built by fine-tuning LLaMA on synthetic instruction data generated with the Evol-Instruct method.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as the primary model produced by the paper's Evol-Instruct pipeline and evaluated against Alpaca, Vicuna, ChatGPT, and other open-source LLMs on automatic benchmarks and human evaluation.

findings.finding_summary: WizardLM-13b outperformed same-sized open-source baselines on a broad set of academic and reasoning benchmarks. Reported scores were Avg.=58.96, MMLU=52.92, ARC=57.25, HellaSwag=80.88, TruthfulQA=50.55, compared with Vicuna-13b Avg.=54.60 and Alpaca-13b Avg.=43.44.
findings.measure: Automatic benchmark scores on MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, and overall average

findings.finding_summary: WizardLM-13b showed stronger code and mathematical reasoning performance than open-source baselines. It achieved HumanEval pass@1=24.0 and GSM8k pass@1=37.15, versus Vicuna-13b HumanEval=12.5 and GSM8k=24.34, and Alpaca-13b HumanEval=9.2 and GSM8k=8.35.

On LLM-judge evaluations, WizardLM-13b exceeded other open-source models but remained below ChatGPT-3.5. Reported scores were AlpacaEval=75.31, MT-Bench=6.35, and WizardEval=89.1, compared with Vicuna-13b AlpacaEval=70.43, MT-Bench=6.21, WizardEval=86.9.
findings.sample_size: WizardEval n=218; AlpacaEval and MT-Bench sample_size=not_reported

findings.finding_summary: In blind human pairwise comparison on WizardEval, WizardLM achieved significantly better results than Alpaca and Vicuna, supporting the effectiveness of Evol-Instruct. The human evaluation used 10 annotators ranking responses on relevance, knowledgeable, reasoning, calculation, and accuracy; all Kappa scores were greater than 0.6.
findings.measure: Blind human ranking/win-rate comparison on WizardEval using relevance, knowledgeable, reasoning, calculation, and accuracy criteria

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's named conversational large language model used for dialogue, instruction following, and text generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in this paper as a baseline model for benchmark comparison and also as the API model used to generate evolved instructions and responses during dataset construction.

findings.finding_summary: As a benchmark comparator, ChatGPT-3.5 achieved the highest reported scores among listed 13B/open-source baselines and WizardLM on the main benchmark table. Reported scores were Avg.=76.15, MMLU=70.0, ARC=85.2, HellaSwag=85.5, TruthfulQA=47.0, HumanEval=48.1, GSM8k=80.8, AlpacaEval=89.37, MT-Bench=7.94, and WizardEval=100.0.
findings.measure: Automatic benchmark scores and LLM-judge scores across nine benchmarks
findings.sample_size: HumanEval n=164; GSM8k n=1319; WizardEval n=218

identified_tools.name: Alpaca
identified_tools.description: A named open-source instruction-following model derived from LLaMA and trained on self-instruct style synthetic instructions.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a named baseline model for comparison with WizardLM, including a retrained Alpaca-13b baseline expanded to 70k instructions.

findings.finding_summary: Alpaca-13b underperformed WizardLM-13b across the main benchmark suite. Reported scores for Alpaca-13b were Avg.=43.44, MMLU=46.63, ARC=51.20, HellaSwag=76.31, TruthfulQA=41.62, AlpacaEval=33.25, MT-Bench=4.78, and WizardEval=76.6.
findings.measure: Automatic benchmark scores and LLM-judge scores across nine benchmarks

findings.finding_summary: Alpaca-13b showed weaker code and mathematical reasoning than WizardLM-13b. Reported scores were HumanEval pass@1=9.2 and GSM8k pass@1=8.35, far below WizardLM-13b's 24.0 and 37.15 respectively.

identified_tools.name: Vicuna
identified_tools.description: A named open-source chatbot model based on LLaMA and fine-tuned on ShareGPT user-shared conversations.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a named baseline for comparison with WizardLM on benchmark and human evaluations.

findings.finding_summary: Vicuna-13b performed below WizardLM-13b on the overall benchmark suite. Reported scores for Vicuna-13b were Avg.=54.60, MMLU=50.84, ARC=51.71, HellaSwag=79.94, TruthfulQA=52.68, AlpacaEval=70.43, MT-Bench=6.21, and WizardEval=86.9, compared with WizardLM-13b Avg.=58.96 and WizardEval=89.1.
findings.measure: Automatic benchmark scores and LLM-judge scores across nine benchmarks

findings.finding_summary: Vicuna-13b was weaker than WizardLM-13b on coding and math reasoning. It scored HumanEval pass@1=12.5 and GSM8k pass@1=24.34 versus WizardLM-13b's HumanEval=24.0 and GSM8k=37.15.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an ML systems conference paper evaluating LLMs on benchmark tasks and human judgments, not an education intervention study with K-12 causal or quasi-experimental methodology. It provides empirical comparisons, but not education-specific impact evaluation or learner-outcome causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear positive benchmark gains for WizardLM over other open-source LLMs, but no standardized education effect sizes or direct student learning impacts are reported. Impact is therefore promising but unclear for education outcomes.
